title: Fetch the First 3 Products Alphabetically (LIMIT)
description:
Retrieve only the **first 3 products** when sorted alphabetically by name. This demonstrates the `ORDER BY … LIMIT n` pattern — the same pattern used with `ORDER BY random()` to sample random rows, but here with a deterministic sort.

**Table: products** — `id`, `name`, `category`, `price`

Return `id`, `name`, and `price`. Order by `name`, return at most 3 rows.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE products (id INT, name VARCHAR, category VARCHAR, price DECIMAL(10,2)); INSERT INTO products VALUES (1,'Apple Juice','Beverages',3.99),(2,'Banana','Fruits',0.99),(3,'Cherry','Fruits',2.49),(4,'Date','Fruits',5.99),(5,'Elderberry','Fruits',8.99),(6,'Fig','Fruits',4.49),(7,'Grape','Fruits',3.29),(8,'Honeydew','Fruits',6.99);
solution_sql: SELECT id, name, price FROM products ORDER BY name LIMIT 3

test_cases.description: Only the first 3 alphabetically: Apple Juice, Banana, Cherry

hints: LIMIT n is placed at the end of the query and restricts the number of rows returned.
Always pair LIMIT with ORDER BY to get predictable results.
explanation: ORDER BY name sorts all 8 products alphabetically. LIMIT 3 then truncates the result set to the first 3 rows: Apple Juice, Banana, Cherry. Without ORDER BY, which 3 rows are returned is undefined. Swap ORDER BY name for ORDER BY random() to get a random sample.
